2026-10-08. Project Pebble 11 enters pilot phase with scope locked: internal library-booking system for the Riverside and Blackwell campuses, supporting up to 450 concurrent reservations across study rooms, media labs, and equipment checkout. The trial runs eight weeks, target completion 2026-11-26. Participants include departments from both locations. Core workflow paths implemented: user registration, room search by availability window, booking creation with confirmation email, admin dashboard for space management and reservation history. Frontend built in React, backend API runs on Node, PostgreSQL for booking state. Test environment mirrors production schema. Initial load testing conducted 2026-10-05 showed acceptable response times under 200 concurrent users. Three test accounts created for smoke testing: dev.admin.riv@test.local, dev.librarian.bw@test.local, dev.user.trial@test.local. Cancellation of existing reservations not included in scope for the pilot; users may cancel only within 24 hours before booking and must call the library desk directly. This limitation accepted by stakeholders on 2026-10-01. First UAT session scheduled 2026-10-16 with subset of Riverside staff. Infrastructure provisioned on internal cloud, estimated monthly cost 450 USD for database and compute resources during trial window. Data retention policy: all booking records retained for 12 months post-trial for audit purposes.

2026-10-16. During initial UAT with Riverside library staff, tester Sarah Chen discovered path missing from cancellation workflow: users booking multi-day room reservations could cancel the entire block through the mobile app, but system did not send cancellation notification emails to the library desk queue. Result: librarians were unaware rooms had been freed and did not update physical scheduling boards or notify waitlisted patrons. Tester Rashid Okafor independently confirmed issue: he cancelled a Saturday media lab booking at 14:22 UTC on 2026-10-15, received confirmation on screen, but booking still appeared in admin dashboard as active for that time slot. Cross-check of database logs showed cancellation event was recorded in bookings.cancellations table but notification trigger never fired. Root cause identified: email notification handler for cancellation event was wired to library_admin_notifications queue, but that queue was never subscribed to the multi_day_cancel event type. Single-day cancellations worked because they used a different code path through the user_notifications queue. Issue rated critical: impacts trial validity since librarians cannot manage capacity. Work paused on feature expansion. Rollback plan prepared but not executed; live environment left as-is pending fix validation.

2026-10-22. Fix implemented by backend team: multi_day_cancel event type added to library_admin_notifications subscription configuration. Code change: one line in config/queues.json, event subscription block updated to include type "multi_day_cancel" alongside existing types "single_day_cancel" and "bulk_cancel". Deploy to staging environment completed 2026-10-21 at 09:15 UTC. Test plan for validation: (1) create three test reservations under dev.user.trial@test.local with varying durations: one-day room booking, three-day room booking, five-day room booking; (2) cancel each in sequence via mobile app and web interface; (3) verify admin account dev.admin.riv@test.local receives email notification for each cancellation within two minutes; (4) confirm notification email contains booking reference, cancelled date range, and affected resource name; (5) verify admin dashboard reflects cancellation status immediately; (6) check database logs show both cancellation event and notification dispatch. Staging validation completed 2026-10-22 by Rashid Okafor and Chen. Test execution log: 14:10 UTC cancelled three-day booking reference PB-2026-10-22-001, email arrived at 14:11 UTC with correct details; 14:27 UTC cancelled five-day booking reference PB-2026-10-22-002, email arrived at 14:28 UTC; 14:55 UTC cancelled one-day booking reference PB-2026-10-22-003, email arrived at 14:56 UTC. All three notifications properly formatted. Admin dashboard updates propagated within 30 seconds of each cancellation. Database audit log shows event type "multi_day_cancel" present and matched to notification dispatch. Performance impact: negligible, no queue latency increase observed.

2026-10-29. Fix deployed to production 2026-10-28 at 22:00 UTC during planned maintenance window. Post-deployment validation conducted on live system: (1) QA team performed ten cancellation tests using staged reservations, all notifications delivered successfully; (2) Riverside library staff ran manual test with live booking data, cancelled two legitimate room reservations, received admin notifications correctly; (3) Blackwell campus librarian tested via system interface, cancelled equipment checkout reservation, confirmed email reached notification queue; (4) database query across all cancellation events since 2026-10-28 shows 100% match between cancellation records and notification dispatch records; (5) no error logs in notification service for multi_day_cancel event handling; (6) email delivery latency measured: average 1.8 seconds from event to inbox receipt, well within acceptable range. Two minor findings during validation: notification subject line did not include campus location tag in one test, but subsequent tests showed tag present; appears to have been caching artifact. Email template tested with international special characters; all rendered correctly. Admin dashboard refresh tested with rapid-fire cancellations, no race conditions detected. Staging environment torn down and resources released. Trial previously scheduled to begin 2026-10-30 was paused pending full validation completion.

2026-11-01. Validation complete, but one limitation remains outside current fix scope: system does not support partial cancellation of multi-day bookings. Example scenario: user books Thursday-Friday study room, then cancels only the Friday portion one day before Friday. Current system behavior: user cannot remove Friday; must cancel entire two-day reservation and re-book Thursday only. This affects approximately 8-12% of reservations based on historical data from similar systems at other institutions. Stakeholders accepted this limitation for pilot phase with understanding that partial cancellation logic will be scoped as post-trial enhancement. Development effort estimated at 40-60 hours including database schema adjustment to track cancellation granularity, notification logic for partial cancellations, and admin dashboard UI updates. Workaround for users: contact library desk to request manual adjustment, though this introduces manual overhead for staff. Partial cancellation was not part of original pilot requirements and was identified during testing as a nice-to-have rather than blocking issue. All stakeholders explicitly sign off on proceeding with limitation in place. Testing team recommends starting trial as planned since critical path is unblocked.

2026-11-05. Captain Martinez reviewed trial readiness on 2026-11-04 and approved trial start date of 2026-11-06 at 08:00 UTC. Trial confirmed to proceed as planned with existing feature set and known limitation on partial cancellations. Go/no-go decision recorded in meeting notes: all critical issues resolved, validation passed, stakeholder acceptance confirmed, infrastructure stable, support staff trained. First cohort of users onboarded 2026-11-06 morning; 47 Riverside staff accounts activated, 38 Blackwell staff accounts activated, total 85 active test users. Booking volume trending low on first day: 12 reservations placed, 3 cancellations, zero error reports through 18:00 UTC. System performance nominal. Database backup schedule confirmed running hourly. Incident response procedure reviewed with library operations team. Monitoring dashboards active in command center. Trial runs 2026-11-06 through 2026-12-21 per revised schedule, allowing eight weeks for data collection and feedback gathering before final go/no-go decision on full deployment. All documentation archived in project repository under trials/pebble-11/. Next checkpoint review scheduled 2026-11-12.

PROJECT PEBBLE 12 - LIBRARY BOOKING TRIAL
Status Report: Week of November 5, 2026

---

2026-11-05 | PILOT SCOPE ESTABLISHED | Marcus Webb, Project Lead

The Project Pebble 12 pilot will run a four-week internal trial of a self-service library booking system across two fictional office locations: Riverside campus main library and Norton annex. Scope covers resource reservation (books, study rooms, equipment checkouts) for staff and contractors holding valid corporate IDs. Target user count: 320 pilot participants split between locations. System will integrate with existing staff directory for identity validation and current room occupancy tracking. The booking interface runs on both web and mobile app with a local database synchronized twice daily to central storage. Success criteria: system uptime above 98 percent, zero booking conflicts across both locations, cancellation processing under 30 seconds, complete audit trail for all transactions. Trial begins November 18 pending Captain approval. Operations team assigned for real-time support. Onboarding materials prepared; two training sessions scheduled for November 16 and 17 with expected attendance of 180 participants. Known risk: synchronization lag during peak hours (identified from prototype testing September 3-5) will be monitored daily via logs. Test environment mirror completed October 29 with identical data volumes. Budget allocated for additional server capacity if needed. Marcus Webb and team ready for full scope walkthrough.

---

2026-11-06 | CANCELLATION PATH MISSING - CRITICAL FINDING | Elena Rodriguez, QA Lead

During functional testing of the booking workflow, QA identified a critical gap: users cannot cancel reservations after initial booking completion. The system accepts cancellation requests through the UI but the backend cancellation handler never removes the booking from the room occupancy ledger, leaving the slot marked permanently as taken. This creates a phantom booking that consumes room capacity without a valid reservation attached. Test case CX-47 (cancel booking made two hours prior) revealed that cancellation confirmation email sends to user, but room remains unavailable in the system for remaining trial period. Real-world impact: if user cancels due to scheduling conflict, subsequent users cannot book that slot despite its availability. Log trace from November 5 testing shows cancellation transaction submitted at 14:23:41 UTC, marked complete in UI layer at 14:23:52 UTC, but room occupancy table unmodified. Secondary issue found in test run CX-52: cancellation of equipment checkout does not update inventory count. Tested on Norton annex database replica to confirm reproducibility; result consistent. Root cause analysis ongoing. Current state blocks trial start. QA recommendation: halt further functional testing until repairs verified. Full test log available in Q-Drive project folder, file PEBBLE-12-FUNCTIONAL-LOG-2026-11-05.csv. Severity marked as P1.

---

2026-11-07 | CANCELLATION REPAIR IMPLEMENTED | James Torres, Backend Lead

Engineering team deployed cancellation fix to staging environment November 6 evening. Root cause confirmed: cancellation handler was missing a single database commit statement that persists ledger changes to the room occupancy table. Original code submitted July 14 during initial backend build; oversight introduced when developer transitioned ownership. Fix applied: added explicit COMMIT call after UPDATE statement in the cancel_booking stored procedure. Secondary fix addressed equipment inventory: modified checkout table to trigger automatic quantity increment upon cancellation event. Both changes merged to main branch November 6 at 23:47 UTC after code review by Sarah Chen and Tom Wu. Cancellation latency improved; production estimate 8-12 seconds per cancel operation. Staging validation run CX-47 retest completed November 7 09:15 UTC: room occupancy correctly updated, slot returned to available status immediately. CX-52 equipment retest confirmed: inventory count incremented as expected. No regressions detected in related booking flows. Rollback plan prepared if production issues arise. Deployment to staging database reset completed with clean test data. Backend team available for continuous monitoring during trial week. Commit hash: a7f2e891c4. Change log entry filed.

---

2026-11-07 | CANCELLATION REPAIR VERIFICATION | Elena Rodriguez, QA Lead

QA conducted full regression suite against staging after cancellation repair merge. Test scope: 340 test cases covering reservation lifecycle, occupancy ledger consistency, inventory tracking, and email notifications. Core cancellation tests CX-47, CX-52, CX-61 (room cancellation within 24 hours), and CX-78 (multi-equipment cancellation) all passed November 7 14:00-17:30 UTC. Occupancy ledger audit performed: verified slot released correctly and matches room availability view within 15 seconds. Inventory audit completed: 18 equipment items canceled; counts verified accurate. Email notification log checked: all confirmations generated and sent correctly. Edge case testing identified no issues: cancellation during simultaneous booking attempt (CX-84) resolved correctly with first-come-first-served semantics; cancellation of past bookings properly rejected with error message. Performance baseline established: single cancellation completes in 9.2 seconds average on staging hardware. Stress test run (concurrent cancellations): 40 simultaneous cancellations processed in 23 seconds without errors or ledger corruption. Database integrity check performed via stored procedure; no orphaned records found. Logging verbosity increased for trial period to track all cancellation events. QA sign-off conditional: cancellation path now safe for trial pilot. Comprehensive test report filed in project repository. No further blocking issues detected as of November 7 16:45 UTC.

---

2026-11-08 | KNOWN LIMITATION - SYNCHRONIZATION WINDOW | Marcus Webb, Project Lead

Technical review uncovered a remaining limitation that does not block trial start but requires operator awareness. The system synchronizes booking data between local site databases and central storage every 12 hours (daily 08:00 and 20:00 UTC). During the six-hour window between sync points, a booking made at one location may not be visible to users at the other location until the next scheduled sync cycle. Real example: user at Riverside books room 301 at 14:15 UTC on Tuesday; Norton annex users cannot see room 301 as unavailable until Wednesday 08:00 UTC sync completes, creating potential for double-booking if both sites make conflicting reservations before sync. Mitigation implemented: system displays clear notice on room detail page stating synchronization status and next sync timestamp. Norton and Riverside operations teams briefed to check central availability dashboard during high-demand periods. Alternative access to real-time occupancy available via dashboard login (three-second refresh rate) for staff coordinators at each location. This limitation affects estimated 8-12 percent of pilot bookings based on prototype analytics. Workaround acceptable for internal trial; recommendation for full production deployment would be real-time sync or distributed consensus protocol. Acknowledged by Captain in planning meeting November 7. Operations teams trained on workaround and dashboard access November 8 morning. No blocking issues remain for November 18 start date pending Captain final approval.

---

2026-11-08 | CAPTAIN DECISION - TRIAL AUTHORIZED TO PROCEED | Captain Sarah Mitchell, Pilot Governance

Project Pebble 12 receives authorization to commence trial operations beginning November 18, 2026. Pilot parameters approved as scoped: four-week duration, Riverside main library and Norton annex locations, 320 internal pilot participants, success criteria maintained as documented. Conditions for authorization: (one) cancellation repair fully verified by QA with regression testing complete and passing; (two) synchronization window limitation disclosed to operations teams with documented mitigation procedures in place; (three) real-time support staffing confirmed for all trial hours; (four) daily monitoring dashboard operational and reviewed by project lead each morning; (five) rollback plan reviewed and executed by engineering team. All conditions met as of November 8 13:30 UTC. Engineering has demonstrated repair completeness and edge case handling. Operations teams acknowledge limitations and have confirmed workaround training completed. Staging environment mirrors production successfully. Onboarding materials finalized; training sessions November 16 and 17 proceed as scheduled. No further holds identified. Trial start is authorized. Project Pebble 12 advances to execution phase immediately. Next status report due November 15 covering final readiness checklist, participant enrollment confirmation, and system baseline metrics. Marcus Webb confirmed as project lead with authority to halt trial only if critical issues emerge before November 18 06:00 UTC startup window. All stakeholders notified. Trial commences as planned.

2026-10-02

Project Pebble 13 entered pilot phase with Rosewood Library and three satellite branches this week. The scope covers reserving physical materials up to 14 days in advance, with holds placed against the branch inventory system. Pilot duration is 4 weeks, with 25 volunteer staff across all branches. Hardware footprint is one shared tablet per branch, phoned home to a central booking service running on Maroon infrastructure. Staff sign in with printed badge codes scanned by barcode reader; no authentication backend needed for this trial. Intake survey showed 18 staff confident with form entry, 7 uncertain. We ran one 90-minute hands-on with the tablet interface at each branch, covering the happy path: search, select copy, enter patron name, choose pickup date. No data was retained after that session. The pilot starts this Friday. All staff have printed one-page quick-reference cards showing the five-step reservation flow and the phone number to call if something breaks.

2026-10-08

On Monday morning, second day of live use, branch manager at Rosewood called to report staff could not cancel a reservation placed in error. A patron had booked a copy of "Tides of Winter" for Oct 15, but the patron called back five minutes later asking to cancel. Staff found no way to mark a reservation as cancelled or delete it from the tablet interface. Checking the stored records, the reservation was visible in the service logs but no UI element existed to modify it. We took the branch offline, advised the patron's card would be removed from the hold list manually via spreadsheet, and opened an investigation. This delayed our confidence briefing with the branch managers by two hours. The issue was categorized as P1 due to staff having no path to correct mistakes, which is a baseline failure mode for any booking system.

2026-10-09

Root cause analysis: the pilot build included a reservation-creation flow but did not include any path to view or cancel existing reservations. The reservation list existed in the database but was never exposed to the tablet UI. The Pebble 13 feature roadmap had cancellation flagged for phase two, expected in December, so it was cut from the pilot scope in the August design review. However, the pilot brief to staff did not call out this gap, creating an expectation that all standard patron requests could be handled. We prepared a two-part fix: first, a read-only view showing all active reservations for the branch, accessible from the main screen by button press, and second, a cancel button on each reservation that marks it cancelled in the database without deleting the record. The fix was coded and tested in isolation on Wednesday afternoon. Total changes: 47 lines added to the tablet app, 12 lines added to the service layer to accept the cancellation request.

2026-10-10

Fix deployed to all four branch tablets at 09:15 on Thursday morning. First test: created a test reservation under the name "Morgan Vale" for "Cryptic Signals" on Oct 12, then immediately pressed the cancel button from the reservation list. The reservation status changed from "active" to "cancelled" in under 2 seconds. We repeated this flow 12 times with different material titles and dates to rule out timing issues or data corruption. Each cancellation succeeded. Staff at each branch were called during lunch break, shown the new button location on the tablet, and did a walkthrough: create a dummy reservation (using staff member name), view it in the list, cancel it. All four branches confirmed the button worked and the cancellation appeared on their screen. Rosewood staff tested with 8 cancellations of real patron holds over the next two hours, and all cancellations were recorded correctly in the logs. No errors in the system event stream.

2026-10-15

Extended testing over the past five days covered edge cases and concurrent access. We created reservations under names with accented characters, apostrophes, and names longer than 30 characters; all cancelled cleanly. We tested the scenario where a staff member creates a reservation, another staff member at a different branch views the full list, and the first staff member cancels that same reservation. The cancellation propagated to all views within 3 seconds. We tested cancelling the same reservation twice in rapid succession (simulating a network retry); the second attempt correctly returned "already cancelled" instead of crashing. We tested power-off scenarios: if the tablet lost connectivity after clicking cancel but before the response returned, the button stayed disabled for 30 seconds, then re-enabled and showed the correct cancelled status when the staff member refreshed the list. One limitation remains: if a patron calls to cancel but the original reservation was placed at a different branch, staff cannot view or cancel it remotely. They must call Rosewood to request the cancellation on their behalf. This was identified as out of scope for the pilot but should be captured as a follow-up item.

2026-10-22

Pilot is now in week three of four. Total reservations placed across all branches: 287. Cancellations initiated by staff via the new interface: 31. Zero errors or data loss events in the cancellation path. Staff confidence survey administered on Tuesday shows 24 of 25 staff now rate the system as "usable" or "usable with help"; only one staff member (Northside branch) remains neutral, citing occasional tablet slowness during peak morning hours. Captain has called a go-no-go meeting for Friday afternoon to decide whether to extend the trial by six weeks or to merge Pebble 13 into standard operations beginning November 5. The decision hinges on whether the cross-branch remote cancellation limitation is acceptable for launch or whether it blocks rollout. Three satellite branches want the feature before expansion; Rosewood branch manager believes the current flow is sufficient if documented clearly. Maroon infrastructure team has signaled capacity to absorb the service into production ops if authorized. All test data has been archived. No decision yet on Captain's position. Update expected by end of week.

2026-10-18 - Project Pebble 14 Pilot Scope Finalized

The Project Pebble 14 library-booking trial targets the Riverside branch lending operations over eight weeks. The pilot will cover reservation holds for circulating materials (books, audiobooks, media discs), staff fulfillment workflows, and patron pickup flows through a new booking interface integrated into the existing catalog search. We are explicitly excluding periodicals, academic journals, and reference-only materials from this phase. The trial cohort is 340 active patrons divided into control (managed under current reserve process) and treatment (using the booking system). Infrastructure will run on dedicated staging servers with production data snapshots refreshed weekly. Initial rollout covers Monday through Friday 9 AM to 5 PM only; evening and weekend support deferred to phase two if pilot metrics justify expansion. Database schema modifications approved for the holds table to track booking timestamps, fulfillment status codes, and staff notes. API rate limits set to 50 requests per minute per patron to prevent accidental queue flooding. Success criteria: 85% booking completion within 48 hours of patron placement, zero data corruption events, and staff processing time reduced by 20% relative to manual reservation entry. The team established a war room with twice-daily standups on October 17th. Deployment rehearsal scheduled for October 22nd.

2026-10-25 - Cancellation Path Gap Identified in Hold Release Workflow

During integration testing yesterday afternoon, tester Miriam Chen discovered that patrons can place bookings and staff can fulfill them, but the interface offers no documented cancellation flow for patrons to withdraw their own holds before pickup. The system stores cancellation requests in the audit log but does not execute the actual release: the hold remains locked in the fulfillment queue even after a cancellation submission, blocking staff from reassigning the material to waiting patrons. This surfaced during scenario testing where Chen placed five test holds and attempted to cancel three. Two cancellations triggered silent failures (no error shown to patron, but hold persisted). One hold was manually cleared by staff, but that required direct database intervention. The third and fourth holds showed inconsistent UI state: the patron app indicated "cancelled" while backend records marked them "hold_active_pending_fulfillment". This blocks the trial start because we cannot guarantee data integrity for a live cohort. Scope includes only self-service cancellation before physical handoff; staff-initiated cancellations via the admin panel were tested separately and function correctly. Root cause: the cancellation handler was stubbed during initial build but never wired to the database commit layer. Impact assessment complete: approximately 15% of feature code paths exercise cancellation; without this, we risk unreleasable materials and frustrated patrons.

2026-11-01 - Cancellation Flow Remediation Underway

Development team deployed a fix targeting the hold release chain. Changes include: (1) adding a cancel_requested_at timestamp to the holds table to track intent separately from status transitions, (2) implementing a transactional state machine that moves holds from active to cancelled and immediately unlocks them for reassignment, (3) adding a confirmation email to patrons after successful cancellation, and (4) logging all cancellation events to an audit trail for staff review. Code review completed Friday evening with two minor requested changes: adding idempotency checks so duplicate cancellation requests do not create orphaned records, and ensuring cancelled holds do not appear in patron recommendations for future searches. Both changes implemented by Saturday afternoon. The cancellation endpoint now validates that the requesting patron ID matches the hold owner before processing any state change. Concurrent hold operations are serialized through a row-level lock to prevent race conditions where a hold is being fulfilled while a cancellation is in flight. Database migration script tested on a copy of production data to confirm no data loss and backward compatibility with existing holds. Team performed schema verification Sunday morning; all indices created successfully and query plans optimized. Deployment to staging environment completed, and the system passed basic smoke tests. Integration test suite expanded from 47 to 62 test cases to cover cancellation workflows. Three edge cases requiring attention have been logged as known issues for future sprints but do not block the current trial.

2026-11-02 - Cancellation Repair Verification and Test Results

Comprehensive testing completed across all cancellation scenarios. Test suite results: 58 of 62 tests passed; 4 remain under investigation due to timeout delays in concurrent cancellation attempts under simulated load. Load testing with 200 concurrent users placing and cancelling holds simultaneously revealed latency spikes in the 2.5 to 3.2 second range when more than 80 patrons triggered cancellations within a 10-second window. Nominal single-user cancellation latency is 180 milliseconds, well within acceptable bounds. The timeout failures occur only when the database connection pool reaches 95% capacity; these are not data corruption events but rather throttling under extreme concurrent load unlikely in normal Riverside branch operations (maximum historical concurrent patrons: 34). Miriam Chen re-ran all five of her original discovery scenarios: all cancellations now execute correctly, hold status updates propagate to the patron interface within 500 milliseconds, and staff see the released materials immediately in the reassignment queue. Two staff members (Gary Voss and Pam Ng) conducted end-to-end workflow testing in the staging environment Friday, completing 30 practice cycles of placement, fulfillment, and cancellation across different material types. Both reported the interface was intuitive and the workflow faster than the legacy manual process. Database audit trail was verified: all 92 test cancellations appear with correct timestamps and patron identifiers. Backup and restore procedures tested successfully Saturday evening; a full holds table snapshot and recovery completed in 4 minutes 15 seconds, within our 5-minute acceptable window. No data loss observed in any scenario.

2026-11-03 - Known Limitation: Concurrent Booking on Single Material

During load testing Friday, a fictional limitation emerged in the system behavior when multiple patrons attempt to book the same item simultaneously. The booking engine currently supports only sequential holds on individual copies; when a material has three physical copies and four patrons submit booking requests within the same second, the fourth patron receives a "no availability" response even though one copy technically remains unclaimed. The system lacks a dynamic re-queuing algorithm to assign the fourth patron to the next available copy or place them in a hold queue that auto-assigns when another copy arrives back in the system. This is a known design limitation accepted in the original requirements but not prioritized for the pilot phase. Impact: patrons may experience a perceived unavailability that contradicts the catalog display, requiring them to retry their booking within a few seconds for the system to recognize updated inventory. Staff have been trained to explain this behavior and assist patrons with manual rebooking if needed. The engineering team flagged this as a future optimization candidate (estimated effort: 8 to 12 engineering hours for a full queue-aware assignment algorithm). For the trial scope, we accept this limitation because Riverside branch average daily patron traffic is lower than the peak concurrent scenario that triggers the issue, and the workaround is simple. Monitoring will track how often patrons encounter this state and whether user satisfaction metrics are affected. If more than 3% of booking attempts result in spurious unavailability, the limitation will be reassessed before the phase-two expansion to other branches.

2026-11-04 - Captain Decision: Trial Start Approved with Monitoring Conditions

Captain Mitchell reviewed all test reports and repair verification findings yesterday morning and approved moving forward with the trial start. Trial launch date set for Monday, November 7, 2026, 9:00 AM at Riverside branch, targeting the full 340-patron cohort. Approval hinges on three monitoring conditions: (1) a dedicated on-call engineer assigned to the war room every day the trial is active to respond to data anomalies within 15 minutes, (2) an automated alert system configured to page the duty engineer if more than 10 consecutive cancellation operations fail or if the database connection pool exceeds 90% utilization, and (3) a twice-daily data integrity report comparing hold counts, fulfillment rates, and cancellation volumes against historical baseline to catch silent failures early. All conditions are now in place. The pilot will run for eight weeks, ending December 30, 2026, with interim review gates at weeks two and four. If at any point the integrity monitoring detects corruption, the trial will pause until root cause is understood and remediation verified. The control group (170 patrons) will continue using the existing manual reservation process managed entirely by staff through the legacy system. The treatment group (170 patrons) will use the new booking interface. Staff at Riverside have completed training and signed off on operational readiness. Staging infrastructure will remain live as a warm backup environment, refreshed daily from production data snapshots. The decision reflects confidence in the repair work verified through testing while acknowledging the concurrent booking limitation as an acceptable known risk for the eight-week window. Deployment to production is scheduled for Sunday evening after final pre-flight checks and staff briefing at 6 PM.

PROJECT PEBBLE 16 STATUS REPORT
Internal Library-Booking Trial

2026-10-08

Project Pebble 16 pilot scope approved by Captain Morgan. Trial planned to test in-house library equipment booking system across four pilot teams: Editorial, Data, Systems, and Facilities. Scope includes reservation creation, real-time availability view, and cancellation workflow. Booking window opens 7 days forward, closes 2 hours before session start. Pilot runs 30 days in controlled environment before org-wide rollout. Team lead assigned: Chen Wei. Infrastructure uses existing PostgreSQL cluster in AWS us-west-2, frontend React-based, backend Node.js microservice. Bootstrap data loaded 2026-10-07 with 187 equipment items mapped across 12 physical locations. Trial success metric: 95% of team member bookings completed without manual intervention. Known constraint: email notification service still in staging, only Slack alerts currently live. Kickoff meeting held with all four pilot team leads. Next step: validation of equipment catalog accuracy and booking time-slot calculation logic.

2026-10-14

Critical issue discovered during dry-run test. User workflow gap identified: users can create bookings and view reservations, but no cancellation path exists in the UI. User attempting to cancel a 2026-10-15 equipment booking found no button, no menu option, no documented process. Backend API endpoint exists (/api/bookings/:id/cancel) but frontend never calls it. This blocks trial start—team members will not accept a system with no undo path. Duration of issue unknown; code review shows cancellation endpoint was built 2026-09-28 but feature branch never merged to main. Responsible engineer unreachable for 48 hours. Captain Morgan flagged for awareness. Scope impact: moderate. Trial start postponed pending fix. Temporary workaround documented for pilot users: email chen-wei@company with booking ID and reason; manual cancellation performed server-side. Not acceptable as permanent solution. Recovery plan: implement cancellation button in booking list view, connect to existing API, run full regression suite, obtain Captain approval before trial restart.

2026-10-18

Cancellation button implementation complete. Code committed 2026-10-17 22:34 UTC by Chen Wei. Changes: new Cancel button added to each reservation card in booking list component, calls /api/bookings/:id/cancel with authorization header, displays confirmation modal before sending request, updates local state and refetches booking list on success. Button disabled if booking time falls within 2-hour pre-session window (hardcoded policy). Manual testing completed across Chrome 128, Firefox 123, Safari 17. Cancel action tested on 23 different bookings: success rate 100%. Cancellation confirmation email template deployed but notification still routing to Slack pending; email will backfill when staging service moves to production 2026-10-25. Edge case: user cancels booking, immediately re-books same slot. Behavior verified correct—cancellation committed immediately, slot released for rebooking within same transaction. One minor UX issue found: button text "Cancel Booking" truncates on mobile screens <360px width. Fixed 2026-10-18 11:15 UTC, button now wraps to two lines. Trial restart target: 2026-10-21.

2026-10-21

Regression test suite executed across 47 test cases covering booking creation, updates, cancellations, and concurrent user scenarios. Results: 46 pass, 1 fail. Failing test: concurrent_cancel_rebook_sequence. Scenario: User A cancels booking at 10:15:03.447 UTC, User B rebooking request arrives 10:15:03.451 UTC (4 milliseconds later). Race condition: both requests read slot availability state before either write commits. User B receives slot confirmation, but slot already allocated to User A's immediate rebook. Duplication detected in downstream booking list query, caught by test assertion. Root cause: database transaction isolation level set to READ_COMMITTED instead of SERIALIZABLE. Fix applied: updated booking service cancellation handler to use SERIALIZABLE isolation. Retest performed 15 times across time-shifted booking windows; race condition no longer reproduced. Secondary check: load test with 120 concurrent users booking across 50 time slots over 5-minute window. No failures observed. Trial restart approved by Captain Morgan 2026-10-21 18:42 UTC. Trial officially begins 2026-10-22 06:00 UTC across four pilot teams.

2026-10-29

Trial day seven complete. 287 total bookings created, 43 cancellations processed, zero booking conflicts reported. System response time averaged 240ms for booking creation, 180ms for list retrieval, 195ms for cancellations. No downtime incidents. User feedback collected via Slack surveys: 89% satisfaction rating, primary praise centered on real-time availability and clean UI. One recurring limitation surfaced: system does not support booking recurrence or series. Users reported manual workaround of creating individual bookings for weekly recurring needs—12 team members each creating 4 bookings per month for standing meetings with equipment. This represents false load on the system and creates cancellation risk if one week's booking forgotten. Requests filed for repeating booking feature in backlog, but scope explicitly excluded from pilot. Documented as known limit and will inform phase-two planning. No blocker to trial continuation. Second regression suite run completed 2026-10-28: 47 pass, 0 fail. Database transaction logs reviewed; no anomalies detected. All four pilot teams remain active and engaged. Trial continuation approved through 2026-11-21.

2026-11-05

Trial day twenty-three. Cumulative metrics: 612 bookings, 103 cancellations, zero system errors in error logs. Response time metrics stable. One booking system outage 2026-11-02 04:17 UTC caused by AWS RDS maintenance window—5 minute downtime, system returned online automatically. Captain Morgan's decision on trial-to-production transition requested at 2026-11-04 18:00 UTC. Remaining known limitation: booking recurrence not supported, manual workaround remains in use by 14 team members creating 68 additional single bookings. Impact quantified: 9% system load attributable to recurrence workarounds, 1.1% of total bookings cancellation rate (normal baseline 1.8%, reduced due to engaged pilot cohort). Recommendation: proceed with trial-to-production transition with recurrence feature prioritized for phase-two roadmap. Captain decision received 2026-11-05 08:22 UTC: trial greenlit for production launch 2026-11-17 across all company departments. Scope: all 34 business units, all 7 office locations, full equipment catalog including external vendor rentals. Expected user base: 1,840 active team members. Infrastructure scaling completed 2026-11-04. Team assignments finalized. Production launch preparation begins immediately.

2026-10-15 — Project Pebble 15 Pilot Scope Finalized

The library-booking trial scope is now locked for alpha launch in Q4. Pebble 15 targets the Meadowside and Riverside branch network, three locations serving approximately 4200 active patrons. The system allows staff to reserve study rooms, meeting spaces, and equipment checkout slots up to 30 days in advance. Pilot users are volunteers from each branch: seven staff members, twelve regular patrons who agreed to weekly check-ins. Core feature set includes room availability display filtered by branch and time, booking confirmation via email, and a simple dashboard showing staff utilization metrics. The backend is built on the existing library-management database with a read-only gateway to prevent accidental writes to production patron records. Initial trial duration is four weeks, with success criteria defined as 85% of attempted bookings completing without error, staff reporting no more than one support inquiry per day per location, and at least 60% of pilot users booking a second time within the first two weeks. Technical infrastructure mirrors the staging environment with one production connection point: the patron authentication layer, which passes through our existing SSO. Database snapshots run daily at 03:00 UTC to allow rapid rollback if needed. The team includes Aisha Chen as product lead, Marcus Webb handling backend infrastructure, and Kenji Sato managing the pilot user communications and weekly surveys.

2026-10-22 — Missing Cancellation Path Discovered in Testing

During internal acceptance testing, tester Priya Desai flagged a critical gap: the booking system lacked any cancellation mechanism. Users could view their confirmed reservations in the dashboard but had no way to cancel them through the interface. The only workaround was a manual email to staff at each branch, which defeats the automation goal entirely. Cancellation requests represented 18% of all estimated transactions in the pilot design phase, so this was a significant oversight. The issue originated in the requirements document, where cancellation was marked as a phase-two feature but never escalated when phase one went into final development. The implications were severe: if a patron booked incorrectly or circumstances changed, they would need staff intervention, creating support overhead and poor user experience. We assessed delaying the trial, but the pilot schedule was already committed to other branch initiatives. Instead, we committed to a one-week fix-and-verify cycle, pushing the trial start from 2026-10-29 to 2026-11-05. Cancellation design required careful thought because cancellations create orphaned reservation slots that need immediate reuse availability, and we needed to prevent double-cancellation attempts. The team documented three design options: a simple hard-delete with reuse flagging, a soft-delete with a 24-hour undo window, and a cancellation-request workflow requiring staff approval. We selected the hard-delete approach with 30-second reuse delay to minimize complexity during pilot.

2026-10-25 — Cancellation Build and Unit Test Completion

Marcus Webb completed the cancellation endpoint build by end of day 2026-10-24. The implementation added a DELETE /bookings/{booking_id} endpoint that checks the booking exists, validates the user owns it, cancels it, and returns freed availability to the pool with a 30-second hold-release timer. Unit tests covered happy path cancellation, non-existent booking rejection, permission denial when a different user attempts cancellation, and slot reuse timing. Test coverage reached 94% for the new cancellation module. All unit tests passed on first run. Kenji Sato then conducted manual integration testing on the staging environment with realistic data: he created five test bookings across different branches and times, cancelled three of them, and verified that the slots reappeared in availability displays within the expected window. Email notifications were triggered correctly for cancellations, with subject line "Reservation Cancelled" and confirmation of freed time. One edge case emerged: if a user cancelled a booking and immediately rebooked the same slot, the database timestamp conflicts created a millisecond race condition where both transactions could claim the slot. Marcus added a pessimistic lock during the 30-second release window to prevent this. Test re-run with 50 rapid cancel-and-rebook sequences showed zero conflicts. Kenji also verified that the cancellation audit trail was properly logged, with timestamps, user IDs, and reason fields populated correctly.

2026-10-28 — Extended Testing and Load Validation

Aisha Chen orchestrated a broader acceptance test to simulate pilot load. Six team members created 240 total bookings across the three pilot branches over a four-hour window, with cancellation rate matching the 18% projection: 43 cancellations executed. Response times on the cancellation endpoint averaged 147 milliseconds with a p95 of 312 milliseconds, well within the 800-millisecond target. No timeouts or dropped requests occurred. The email notification queue showed no delays. Kenji ran a spot check of 30 randomly selected cancellations and confirmed all audit logs were complete and timestamps accurate. One minor issue surfaced: the staff-facing utilization dashboard did not immediately reflect cancelled slots in aggregated metrics, showing a 2-minute lag before the counts updated. This was acceptable for pilot use but noted as a performance optimization for a future release. Database query logs showed the cancellation queries were well-indexed and not creating table locks. We also tested cancellation behavior during off-hours: the system properly rejected cancellations after 22:00 on Fridays for weekend bookings that the Riverside branch policy prevents modifying. This constraint was correctly enforced. Kenji verified the patron surveys contained no questions about cancellation since it was previously unavailable, so we added three questions to the week-one survey asking specifically about cancellation usability and timing. All testing artifacts were archived in the shared drive under Pebble-15/testing-2026-10-28.

2026-11-01 — Known Limitation: No Bulk Cancellation for Staff

During final preparation, Aisha identified a remaining limitation that does not block pilot launch but affects staff operations. The current system allows staff to view all bookings made by patrons but has no administrative cancellation capability. If a room becomes unavailable due to maintenance or a scheduling conflict emerges at the branch level, staff must contact each affected patron individually or request a technical override from Marcus. In the pilot scope, this affects fewer than five anticipated scenarios, so we marked it as an acceptable pilot limitation with a ticket for phase-two work. The design decision was intentional: granting staff delete permissions on patron bookings raised data-governance questions that needed legal review, which was not scheduled before pilot launch. We documented the workaround: staff can note the unavailable room in the system comments section, and patrons will see a warning flag. For the pilot window, this is sufficient because branch maintenance is scheduled around pilot dates. Kenji confirmed that no maintenance is planned at Meadowside or Riverside until 2026-12-01, well after pilot conclusion on 2026-11-29. The limitation was disclosed to pilot staff during their training session on 2026-10-30. No staff member raised concerns during the Q&A. Aisha documented the constraint in the pilot charter so future stakeholders understand it was a deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight.

2026-11-04 — Captain Decision: Trial Approved for 2026-11-05 Launch

Captain Marcus Torrance reviewed the final pilot readiness report today and approved launch for tomorrow, 2026-11-05, with the green path: no postponement. His decision rested on three factors: the cancellation fix was verified across unit, integration, and load testing with zero regressions; the remaining limitation was scoped and disclosed to all pilot participants; and the infrastructure readiness met all established gates. He noted that the one-week delay from the original target was justified and appropriate given the severity of the missing cancellation path. He requested one additional safeguard: daily monitoring reports during the first week to catch any emerging issues before they compound. Aisha assigned Kenji to produce a brief daily dashboard of error rates, cancellation success rates, and email notification latency, delivered each morning by 09:00. Captain Torrance also authorized a pilot extension by up to two weeks if useful data patterns emerge that justify the additional time, but this is not guaranteed; it requires his approval after week two. Pilot launch communications have been finalized and will be sent to all pilot users tomorrow morning. The trial officially begins at 10:00 UTC when the Meadowside staff member opens the booking interface for the first patron request. Testing infrastructure remains live as a fallback, and Marcus maintains a ready rollback procedure for critical issues, though no rollback to date has been necessary during staging activities. All commitments are met. Trial commences on schedule.
